conclusions.basis: munis-school-journal.csv, fund 1312, revenue lines whose description or comment contains ELC.
conclusions.claim: Fees typed “ELC” came to $37,607 in FY2026, of the fund’s $274,325 in fees.
conclusions.detail: 27 of 105 fee deposit lines in FY2026 say ELC, 13.7% of the fund’s fees. A deposit batches many families’ payments, and nothing requires the label.
conclusions.not_shown: How many children, or what the ELC charges: neither is in the ledger, and the portal publishes no rates.
conclusions.so_what: That is a floor for the ELC’s fees, not its total: the label is optional.

conclusions.basis: school-fund-flows.csv (fund 1312), which ties every year to the Town’s period-13 report; the opening balance is the annual report’s.
conclusions.claim: The fund that pays ELC staff spent more than it took in, 3 of 4 years.
conclusions.detail: In FY2026 fees were $274,325 and spending $371,461. The closing balance is carried forward by us from the ledger; the town has not printed it.
conclusions.not_shown: How much of the spending is the ELC and how much Extended Day: they share one payroll account.
conclusions.so_what: By our reckoning it closed FY2026 at -$2,569, which leaves nothing in reserve.

conclusions.basis: School Committee agendas and minutes, the staff directory and the journal; each quoted in the timeline.
conclusions.claim: The ELC handbook came to the School Committee in 5 springs running.
conclusions.detail: Its director is district staff, its fees go to a school revolving fund, and it registers on its own dates, apart from Pre-K.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether the ELC is licensed as child care, or its age range: no document we hold says.
conclusions.so_what: The ELC is a school district programme, run separately from the preschool.

grain: Dollars in the school Extended Day Revolving Fund (fund 1312), which pays for the ELC and Extended Day together, and dated documents that name the ELC.
not_established: How many children attend the ELC, in any year. No document we hold counts them; the Primary School reports its enrolment without them.
What the ELC charges. The payment portal sells it beside Extended Day and publishes no rates, and no fee schedule is in a budget book or a warrant.
What the ELC costs. It shares fund 1312, and its payroll account, with Extended Day, so its spending cannot be separated.
Whether the general fund carries any ELC cost, such as space, utilities or administration, that is not booked to the fund.
Its age range, hours, or whether it is licensed as child care.

timeline.what: The earliest mention we hold: a staff post named for the ELC, and the programme housed at the T.C. Passios building.
The Superintendent lists the ELC and Extended Day among the district’s programmes while discussing space for Pre-K classrooms.
The Town Manager reports the ELC will move to T.C. Passios, and distinguishes it from the integrated preschool.

timeline.body: School Committee agenda, filed under advisory councils
timeline.what: A proposed Extended Day and ELC rate increase is on the agenda.
Extended Day and ELC recommendations and handbooks are on the agenda.
The teen center is ruled out as a home for the ELC because of its play equipment.
The School Committee asks for the Brooks House as an ELC; the design committee expects the programmes to return to school buildings.
Extended Day and ELC handbooks are on the agenda for action.
Pre-K registration and ELC registration open on different dates, as separate programmes.
The Director presents the Extended Day and ELC handbooks: no price or policy changes.
The FY2026 handbooks move the ELC to the Primary School.
The committee adopts the unaffiliated salary schedule, described as mostly Extended Day and ELC staff paid from the revolving fund.
The Primary School reports its enrolment as not including the ELC.
The library’s preschool storytime loses the ELC children after the move.
The FY2027 Extended Day and ELC handbooks are approved; the ELC stays at the Primary School.
Preschool and ELC children start together, the week after kindergarten.
